 Dhokla on Inspired-Saint Relationship: “If You Don’t Let the Stress Out, Nothing Gets Fixed”
 Davide "Dovi" Xu

 LYON have made it to the Worlds 2026 quarterfinals. The LCS team was able to make an insane comeback against LØS in a rollercoaster three-game series. After dropping Game 1 and almost losing the second game, LYON found some game-winning plays to get the victory and will now move on to face Gen.G in the quarterfinals, a team they have already faced in Swiss.
 At the end of the match, LYON Dhokla shared with us how he felt playing the match and his view on the heated relationship between Inspired and Saint.
 Image Credit: Hotspawn/Riot Games 
 Davide : Man, that was insane. What a roller coaster. You were giving every fan a heart attack.
 What was it like playing the series?
 Dhokla : Playing the games was a lot less stressful than watching them, one hundred percent. It was an absolute roller coaster. Game 1 was kind of close, and we got beat. In Game 2, we should have lost; it should have been a 2-0, but somehow we brought it back.
 In Game 3, we should have been winning hard, but they brought it back, and it turned into really close teamfights that we just barely managed to win. Credit to LØS . They’re a really good team and they played well. It took everything we had to win.
 Davide : I want to talk about Game 1… not the game itself, but what we saw in the review room. We saw Inspired seemingly lash out at Saint, although we couldn’t hear the audio.
 Are you willing to share what happened?
 Dhokla : He was upset about the first crab situation , when Alistar showed mid because Inspired was trying to bait the situation. He was also upset with Saint, saying that if you’re winning your lane, you should base and come back onto the map so you’re actually winning, instead of staying pushed in the whole time.
 He was frustrated about all the early-game mistakes. It’s understandable. This is our biggest series of the year, and you don’t want to come away regretting things and saying, “I should have done this” or “I should have done that.” He’s our leader, and that’s just his style.
 Davide : What about Game 2 ? How do you keep your mental locked in when you’re down 8,000 gold? At one point, your only win condition seemed to be Yunara, and she wasn’t even ahead.
 Dhokla : That game was basically about hoping we could scale, and it happened. LeBlanc was unstoppable in the side lane. Ambessa was also unstoppable in the side lane. They had Baron twice and were sieging us with Caitlyn’s Rapid Firecannon.
 I still don’t know how we won that game. It should have been lost. It’s absolutely crazy that we somehow hung on and won when it should have been a 2-0. 
 Davide : Do you think that resilience is a good sign for the team? MKOI, for example, seemed to struggle to come back after losing one game. You showed that resilience against Gen.G and again today against LOS.
 Is that an extra factor that makes LYON one of the better Western teams here?
 Dhokla : It’s definitely one of our strengths. When you’re playing from behind, you have to get creative and choose your plays wisely, because if you make a bad play, the game is over. We hold on until we see a good opportunity, even if other teams might see the opportunity differently or get punished earlier.
 But it’s not an easy position to be in. It’s really hard to decide whether a play will be good for us or whether we’re giving everything away. Sometimes you just have to hold on and turtle as much as you can. It’s a very difficult position.
 Davide : You’re in the top eight now, though you don’t know who you’ll play yet.
 Is there anyone you’d like to face among the 3-0 and 3-1 teams?
 Dhokla : Anyone but Gen.G would be preferable. (Big Dhokes jinxed himself and got GEN in the end…) 
 Davide : Why not Gen.G?
 Dhokla : I think they’re one of the tournament favorites on paper. Between them and Hanwha, based on how they played yesterday, they look like they’re on a completely different level. Obviously, you’d want to avoid the tournament favorites if you can.
 We did have a close series against them, but if I had to choose, I wouldn’t pick them. At this point, you have to play well to keep advancing. The competition is the best it can be, so it’s on you to play well.
 NEW YEAR, NEW DHOKES pic.twitter.com/PjD8k0qYKE 
 — LoL Esports (@lolesports) October 31, 2026 
 Davide : It’s also because you want to get that prize money, right?
 Dhokla : Oh my God, dude. If I get… I don’t know how much I got for making it to top eight, but I’m sure it’s a good amount. Making the semis would be great if we do that.
 Davide : Would that be enough to get a Taycan? Are you a car guy? I heard you want to get a Taycan , and I think you have great taste. What’s a must-have option for you in a car?
 Dhokla : I’ve been looking at the Taycan, and I’ve customized it a bit. I think the paint is important.
 Davide : Which color?
 Dhokla : Honestly, that’s tough to decide because they have a lot of good colors. Once I get closer to that milestone, I’ll settle on something. For now, it’s a good goal to aspire to. We’ll keep going, and we can make it a reality.
 Davide : Speaking of money,
 Do you think money buys happiness?
 Dhokla : It does not. No, because it just doesn’t. I mean, it can save you from despair, but it can get you to a baseline of normal. After that, I don’t think it will bring you happiness over the long term.
 Davide : In the short term, though?
 Dhokla : In the immediate short term, yeah, totally. You can buy anything you want, and you’ll get an instant dopamine hit for a while. But when that wears off, you’re still back at your baseline.
 Davide : So it’s temporary happiness.
 Where does your happiness come from?
 Dhokla : Happiness comes from improving. I love playing League, and I’m very passionate about it, but I also like the process of improving. That’s the big thing for me right now. I’d say it’s my main passion, and I’m glad I get to do this for a living. I’m living my dream right now.
 Image Credit: Riot Games/Hotspawn 
 Davide : Do you think it’s better to be naturally talented, or to work hard enough to reach that level? A lot of the time, you’re striving toward a goal without knowing whether you’ll be able to reach it. But people often find happiness or fulfillment along the way.
 Do you feel the same way?
 Dhokla : I try to. It’s a back-and-forth discussion in my head. Ultimately, life isn’t made up of your big moments, like when you reach a milestone, because those only happen a few times . Most of your life is your day-to-day and how you process it.
 You have to be happy with what you’re doing every day, because that’s the majority of your life.
It’s not like winning Worlds, because that’s only one day.
It’s not your whole life. Your day-to-day has to matter more than your overall goal. 
 Davide : How has your day-to-day been so far?
 Dhokla : Very stressful.
 Davide : Has this Worlds been more stressful than the previous ones?
 Dhokla : Absolutely.
 Davide : Is that because of the expectations, or something else?
 Dhokla : Both. We were coming off MSI, and people saw us as really strong. We were favored to win 2-0. We were in a position to go 2-0 against Gen.G and could have won that series. The series against IG was even more stressful. This whole year has been extremely stressful.
 But you don’t get where you want to go by being comfortable.
You have to go through discomfort. It’s part of the journey. 
 Davide : Do you think the team environment helps you build through that? From the outside, it seems like the conflict between Saint and Inspired might help since you can vent your frustration, and lock in afterward without resentment toward each other.
 Dhokla : I’m not sure. I think it’s good that they have an outlet to let the stress out, because if you don’t do that, nothing gets fixed. Everyone can end up bickering.
 I’ve been on teams where you start resenting someone because they aren’t changing, or because you aren’t speaking up about it. I’ve been in that situation a few times, so I like the vibe of this team. 
 Even though Game 1 looked the way it did, whatever people saw or interpreted in that review room, it still showed that you were trying. Your year was on the line.
 Image Credit: Liu Yicun/Riot Games 
 Davide : It means you care.
 One last message for the fans?
 Dhokla: What an absolute roller coaster. I wouldn’t have blamed you if you started typing “2-0, you guys suck,” because that’s what it looked like in the game. But thank you for the support. Everyone in the stadium was unbelievably loud after we came back, and that was a great moment for us and for me .
 It was a big moment for NA too. I want to thank the fans who came out today. I saw a few people wearing my jersey, which I especially loved. It’s so crazy that people have a jersey with my name on it. Thank you.
